Onboarding.step1Body: Type a keyword in the top-left search — e.g. «register dog», «passport» or «social aid». You'll instantly see the responsible office.
Onboarding.step2Body: The «Machinery» tab shows the whole administration as a network. Hover highlights a unit and its connections, click pins the selection and opens the detail panel.
Onboarding.step3Body: The «Tax franc» tab shows where your money goes — each department as an area, larger = more spending. Click a department to zoom in.

Belege.title: Evidence & provenance
Belege.intro: How reliable is the information on the procedures? This page shows which binding details – deadlines, fees, legal remedies – are backed by a verbatim quote from an official source, and which checks the data goes through. The values themselves are deliberately not shown here, only on the page of each procedure, always with a link to the original source.
Belege.privacyNote: Generated deterministically from the process data — no usage or personal data, no invented values.
Belege.kpiBelegt: binding details with a verbatim quote
Belege.kpiGesetz: quotes taken directly from the legal text (PDF)
Belege.kpiHochrisiko: high-risk procedures, all with a visible notice
Belege.ebenenHeading: Sources of the evidence by level of government

herkunft.redaktionTitel: Compiled editorially: drafts with AI assistance, every item checked by a person
herkunft.tesseraTitel: Structure proposed by the extraction software tessera, checked by a person
herkunft.gemischtTitel: Compiled editorially and supplemented by proposals from tessera, checked by a person
herkunft.nichtErfasstTitel: The origin of this procedure has not been recorded yet

Belege.matrixIntro: One procedure per row, in alphabetical order. The name leads to the evidence on the procedure’s page.
Belege.matrixFolgt: Not yet in the table: the result of the weekly check (link reachable? quote still verbatim on the page? legal version still in force?). It will follow with the first run.
Belege.caption: Evidence per procedure: binding details, verbatim quotes, sources, legal texts and oldest retrieval
Belege.abrufAltTitle: This evidence was retrieved more than a year ago. If in doubt, the official source applies.
Belege.pruefIntro: Every change to the process data goes through these stages. No stage replaces the next, and nothing is published without human approval.

erfassung.name: Capture
erfassung.was: A procedure is compiled editorially or prepared by the tessera software and submitted as a change proposal. A language model is involved on both paths.
erfassung.grenze: Proposals from tessera only supply the structure; existing, reviewed texts and translations are kept. For binding values, a language model’s suggestion does not count: they appear only with a verbatim quote from the official source, checked against the page.

schema.name: Data contract
schema.was: For every proposal, CI checks that the file meets the data contract: required fields, references, high-risk notice and no binding values outside the quotes.
schema.grenze: Checks the form, not whether the content is correct.

regression.name: Protection of existing texts
regression.was: A proposal may not silently empty or remove documented translations and descriptions.
regression.grenze: Exceptions are possible, but only individually justified and approved.

referenzen.name: Evidence check
referenzen.was: For every new or changed binding detail, the linked page is retrieved live: is the link reachable, and is the quote there verbatim?
referenzen.grenze: Existing, unchanged evidence is only checked by the weekly check.

review.name: Human approval
review.was: A person reviews every change before it is published. Nothing is merged automatically.
review.grenze: Whether a quote reflects the detail correctly is judged by a person, not the machine.

woche.name: Weekly check
woche.was: Once a week, all links are retrieved, all quotes are compared with the source again and linked legal texts are matched against the version in force.
woche.grenze: Some authorities block retrieval from the checking environment; blocked does not mean dead. New findings only appear here after a person has accepted them.

methodik.woertlich: “Quoted verbatim” means: the quote appeared exactly like this on the linked official page when it was retrieved. It does not mean the detail has been legally reviewed.
methodik.keineWerte: The binding values themselves are not shown here. They appear only on the procedure’s page, as a quote with a link to the original source.
methodik.herkunft: “Editorial” means: a person worked out the procedure from the official sources. Drafts were produced with AI assistance, and a person checked every item before it was published. “Mixed” means: in addition, the tessera software proposed structure that a person checked and adopted. Binding values never rely on a language model, but always on a verbatim quote from the official source.
methodik.uebersetzung: English, French, Italian and easy language are derived from the German, partly with AI assistance. Review by native speakers and by easy-language specialists is still pending.
methodik.erreichbar: A reachable link does not mean the content is still correct: pages are rewritten, and some only deliver their text in the browser.
methodik.gesperrt: Some authorities block automated retrieval. A blocked retrieval is not a dead link and is never shown as one.
methodik.stand: A finding only applies to the checked version of a detail. If it has been changed since, it counts as open until the next check covers it.
methodik.veroeffentlichung: The weekly check only publishes a new finding when something changes, and only after a person has accepted it. The date names the run that established the current state.
methodik.verbindlich: The official source is always binding. If in doubt, seek personal advice.

Belege.kpiOffen: open findings of the weekly check
